        ### Question
        Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) is a chelating agent widely used as a titrator in complexometric assessments that are characterized by:

        ### Options
        opa. To make possible the EDTA titration of many metals in alkaline solutions an auxiliary complexing agent is used which prevents the metal ion from precipitating as hydroxide.
opb. EDTA forms complexes of 1: 2 stoichiometry with some metal ions and therefore has a poor application in quantitative analysis.
opc. It is important to choose an adequate pH to carry out the titration because metal-EDTA complexes are more stable at low pH than at high pH.
opd. When evaluating a metal ion with EDTA, there is an excess of EDTA at the equivalence point.
ope. When evaluating a metal ion with EDTA, there is an excess of metallic ion at the equivalence point.

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: EDTA is a chelating agent. -> EDTA is widely used as a titrator in complexometric assessments. -> An auxiliary complexing agent is used with EDTA to prevent metal ions from precipitating as hydroxides in alkaline solutions. -> Choosing an adequate pH is important for the stability of metal-EDTA complexes during titration. -> Metal-EDTA complexes are more stable at low pH than at high pH. -> At the equivalence point in EDTA titration, there is an excess of EDTA. -> 95%
CHAIN: EDTA forms complexes of 1:2 stoichiometry with some metal ions. -> This property of EDTA allows for its application in quantitative analysis. -> 80%
CHAIN: When evaluating a metal ion with EDTA. -> There is an excess of EDTA at the equivalence point. -> There is no excess of metallic ion at the equivalence point. -> 90%
